current.text: Yahoo lists him as questionable with an illness.
He is projected to start at guard next to Bane, Franz Wagner, Banchero and Carter. That group was very good when it played together.
Orlando has a new head coach, Sean Sweeney, so player roles may change.
Orlando is 2.5 million USD under the second apron and will likely have to choose between keeping Suggs and keeping Black.
He shot under 30% from the field and in the low 20s from three in the playoffs.
One expert thinks he is the likely trade sacrifice so Orlando can keep Black.
Drafts have him far too low. Experts see him as a top 70 to 80 player per game and worth the shot despite the injury risk.
He is a tier 8 guard. If he plays 65 to 70 games, he would rank ahead of nearly all of tier 8.
A healthy offseason could unlock another level after his career-high assists last season.
He went for 9 USD in an expert auction mock draft.

durable.text: He is injury prone. His physical, all-out style gets his body beaten up, and availability is his main issue.
Plan for him to miss about 20 games a season.
His per game numbers are strong when he plays.
His three-point shooting is streaky. When it is on, he takes about six threes a game.
Steals are his standout category, far above the pool. His blocks are also high for a guard.

note: Experts in 9-cat see him as a top 70 to 80 player per game. The market is far lower: Yahoo rank 95 at 2.3 USD average cost, ESPN rank 143 at 0.6 USD, and he went for 1 USD in our league last auction. One expert mock paid 9 USD, so a bid in the low single digits is a good price for elite steals plus threes and assists, if you can live with weak FG% and turnovers and plan around 20 missed games. Early on, check the illness status, his role under new coach Sweeney, and any trade talk tied to Orlando's choice between him and Black.
